evidence.exact_quote: The OpenCode formatter baseline preserves the built-in formatter catalog and detection table, including prettier, biome, rustfmt, gofmt, ruff, shfmt, clang-format, dart, mix, zig, ktlint, rubocop, standardrb, pint, ocamlformat, nixfmt, ormolu, terraform, latexindent, gleam, cljfmt, oxfmt, uv, air, htmlbeautifier, and dfmt.

items.impact: Implementers can preserve the catalog yet disagree on executable discovery precedence, version support, refresh behavior, and the oracle for a detected formatter.
items.statement: The formatter catalog is explicit, but the detection-table contract, precedence, supported-version policy, and deterministic detection tests are not specified.
items.title: Formatter detection remains non-falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: Formatter config preserves formatter: false global disablement, per-formatter disabled/command/environment/extensions fields, $FILE replacement at execution time, command.length === 0 skip behavior, and config-defined custom formatter enabled() override behavior.

items.impact: Different escaping, environment, timeout, and concurrent-edit choices can create command injection, incorrect file targeting, or partial writes while still satisfying the listed fields.
items.statement: The config shape and skip conditions are explicit, but `$FILE` escaping, environment trust, timeout, exit-code handling, concurrent edits, and rollback behavior are unspecified.
items.title: Formatter execution trust boundary is missing

evidence.exact_quote: Skill discovery preserves the OpenCode load order across external global roots, external project roots, .opencode skill roots, config.skills.paths[], and config.skills.urls[] with Discovery.pull() cache download behavior and later-source overwrite semantics.

items.impact: A remote or later source can silently replace a trusted skill, and implementations can diverge on stale-cache, offline, update, and failure behavior.
items.statement: Load order and overwrite direction are specified, but URL trust, authenticity, cache invalidation, offline use, failed download handling, and overwrite visibility are not.
items.title: Remote skill discovery lacks integrity controls

evidence.exact_quote: Skill frontmatter preserves required name and description fields, auto-set location and content fields, the name regex and length constraints, duplicate overwrite warning behavior, and the compatibility-only fact that license, compatibility, and metadata may appear without core validation.

items.impact: Malformed or duplicated skills can be accepted, rejected, or overwritten differently, with compatibility metadata exposed despite lacking validation.
items.statement: Required fields and name constraints are named, but exact length bounds, validation error disposition, duplicate winner identity, and treatment of unvalidated compatibility metadata are not executable oracles.
items.title: Skill frontmatter validation is incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: Skill agent surface preserves available skill listing through <available_skills> XML blocks, invocation through skill({ name }), and registration as invokable /skillname commands from the command palette.

items.impact: The XML, tool, and command-palette consumers can expose different availability, denial, stale-discovery, and error states, misleading users or agents.
items.statement: Three invocation surfaces are named without a shared availability state model, permission-denial behavior, refresh rule, accessibility contract, or localized display requirement.
items.title: Skill surfaces can disagree about availability

evidence.exact_quote: Skill permission integration preserves the skill permission key with patterns, skill-directory external_directory whitelisting, and compaction protection through PRUNE_PROTECTED_TOOLS = ["skill"].

items.impact: Path normalization, symlinks, pattern conflicts, and compaction can broaden authority or retain unusable tool state inconsistently.
items.statement: Permission keys and protection are named, but pattern resolution, external-directory canonicalization, symlink handling, conflict precedence, revocation, and compaction-time permission validity are unspecified.
items.title: Skill permission boundary is underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: Plugin discovery preserves internal auth plugins, the built-in opencode-anthropic-auth@0.0.13 package, config.plugin[] package or file:// entries, BunProc.install(), import(plugin), and Set<PluginInstance> deduplication.

items.impact: Network or local plugins can execute with undefined trust, integrity, lifecycle, and rollback controls, exposing credentials, files, and subprocess authority.
items.statement: Discovery and deduplication are explicit, but package authenticity, version locking beyond one built-in, file URL trust, installation atomicity, sandboxing, update/revocation, and failed-import recovery are absent.
items.title: Plugin loading has no defined trust model

evidence.exact_quote: Plugin context preserves the async PluginInput signature with client, project, worktree, directory, serverUrl, and $ fields, where $ is the Bun shell for subprocess execution and the plugin returns a Hooks object.

items.impact: A plugin can receive project, network, client, and shell capabilities without specified attenuation, secret handling, cancellation, or failure isolation.
items.statement: The API signature is explicit, but capability scoping, lifetime, mutability, authentication data exposure, subprocess restrictions, cancellation, and invalid Hooks handling are undefined.
items.title: PluginInput exposes unbounded capabilities

evidence.exact_quote: Plugin hook events preserve event, config, tool, auth, chat.message, chat.params, chat.headers, permission.ask, command.execute.before, tool.execute.before, tool.execute.after, shell.env, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.session.compacting, and experimental.text.complete.

items.impact: Plugins can observe or mutate the same operation in different orders and failures can leave configuration, permissions, messages, or tool state partially transformed.
items.statement: The hook catalog is complete as a list, but payload contracts, ordering, concurrency, timeout, cancellation, mutation composition, error propagation, and rollback are unspecified.
items.title: Plugin hook lifecycle is not defined

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode plugin custom tools are defined through the tool hook property, loaded into ToolRegistry beside built-ins, and override built-in tools on name collision as the baseline extensibility behavior.

items.impact: A plugin can shadow a privileged built-in, and multiple plugin collisions can resolve nondeterministically unless the PM divergence is explicitly enforced at the registry boundary.
items.statement: The OpenCode baseline permits implicit built-in override, but precedence among multiple plugins, user disclosure, permission inheritance, and the seam to PM's later `override_builtin: true` rule are not specified here.
items.title: Tool override precedence crosses an authority seam

evidence.exact_quote: Provider model ID parsing preserves provider_id/model_id format and parseModel() split-on-first-slash behavior, with everything before the first slash as providerID and the joined remainder as modelID.

items.impact: Blank, slash-free, whitespace, case-variant, or Unicode identifiers can be accepted or rejected inconsistently and select unintended providers or models.
items.statement: The first-slash split is deterministic for valid examples, but validation, normalization, escaping, empty components, and error behavior are not defined.
items.title: Model ID parser lacks invalid-input rules

evidence.exact_quote: Default model selection preserves config.model priority, model.json last-used lookup, internal priority list gpt-5, claude-sonnet-4, big-pickle, gemini-3-pro, latest suffix sorting, model ID sorting, and the note that CLI flag override occurs upstream.

items.impact: Unavailable or retired models, corrupt last-used state, and an upstream CLI override can yield inconsistent defaults across consumers.
items.statement: Priority inputs are listed, but the total precedence including CLI, invalid model.json recovery, unavailable-model fallback, capability filtering, and persistence update timing are not defined.
items.title: Default model fallback is incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: Provider-specific model options preserve config.provider.<provider>.options, Anthropic beta headers, OpenAI .responses() API use, Bedrock region/profile/credentials, and per-agent model overrides through agent.<name>.model.

items.impact: Provider adapters can expose credentials, accept incompatible options, or resolve per-agent overrides differently across APIs.
items.statement: Provider option locations and examples are named, but schemas, validation, credential sourcing/redaction/lifetime, beta-header ownership, and invalid per-agent override recovery are unspecified.
items.title: Provider options lack secret and validation rules

evidence.exact_quote: Model variants preserve built-in and custom variants, UI keybind cycling, and per-agent variant overrides through agent.<name>.variant.

items.impact: Cycling can select unsupported or stale variants without communicating the effective per-agent override, creating misleading requests.
items.statement: Keybind cycling is specified, but order, wraparound, capability filtering, invalid custom variants, effective-state display, keyboard conflict, screen-reader feedback, and localization are not.
items.title: Variant cycling lacks observable selection semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Provider transform baseline preserves normalizeMessages(), providerOptions(), schema() compatibility transforms, maxOutputTokens(), OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX, and OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX.

items.impact: Provider migrations or token-limit configuration can silently alter messages, schemas, or truncation without a versioned compatibility oracle.
items.statement: Transform entry points and limit names are preserved, but per-provider input/output invariants, transform composition, failure atomicity, numeric bounds, precedence, and golden tests are missing.
items.title: Provider transforms are named but not testable

evidence.exact_quote: Provider error handling preserves isOverflow() regex detection across provider error messages, isRetryable() provider-specific retryability including OpenAI 404 handling, and nested responseBody JSON error extraction.

items.impact: Regex or provider-specific misclassification can retry permanent errors, repeat non-idempotent work, suppress actionable failures, or exhaust resources.
items.statement: Overflow and retry classifiers are named, but precedence, retry budgets, backoff/jitter, idempotency, cancellation, malformed responseBody handling, and observable terminal errors are not.
items.title: Provider retries lack bounded recovery semantics

evidence.exact_quote: The DRY mapping routes run modes, agent switching, approval semantics, agent definitions, subagent invocation, explore agent, prompt assembly, compaction, permissions, and commands to their owning Puppet Master SSOT docs rather than duplicating definitions here.

items.impact: Builders can follow different owners for tightly coupled run, agent, approval, prompt, permission, and command behavior, leaving seams or circular authority unresolved.
items.statement: The map establishes non-duplication and names owner-doc categories, but it does not bind each topic to a versioned contract, define seam precedence, or supply cross-owner consistency oracles.
items.title: Run and agent SSOT seams lack adjudication

evidence.exact_quote: The DRY mapping routes formatter, skill, plugin, and model extraction topics to Formatters_System, Skills_System, Plugins_System, and Models_System owner docs.

items.impact: This prevents the extraction document from becoming a competing SSOT for formatter, skill, plugin, or model behavior.
items.statement: The owner boundary is explicit: the named system documents retain canonical behavior and this extraction document only routes topics.
items.title: Formatter, skill, plugin, and model ownership is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: The DRY mapping routes Tools plus ToolContext, normalized provider stream, storage event types, and message/part taxonomy to Tools.md, Contracts_V0.md, CLI_Bridged_Providers.md, storage-plan.md, and related owners.

items.impact: The same provider stream, message part, tool context, or storage event can be normalized or owned differently across multiple documents.
items.statement: Several owner documents are named, but `related owners` is open-ended and no field-level producer/consumer mapping, precedence, or integration oracle is supplied.
items.title: Tool-provider-storage ownership is not closed-world

evidence.exact_quote: The DRY mapping routes UI commands to Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md and preserves the ContractRef set for EventRecord, UICommand, bridged providers, Provider_OpenCode, Tools, UI_Command_Catalog, and storage-plan.

items.impact: Stable references can all exist while event, command, provider, tool, and storage schemas disagree at their producer-consumer seams.
items.statement: The UI command owner and ContractRef set are explicit, but compatibility/version rules, required callers and consumers, propagation guarantees, and cross-contract validation are absent.
items.title: UI command ContractRefs lack seam validation

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master plan-mode deltas preserve Rust-native plan mode, Rust prompt-builder reminder injection, and plan file locations at global ~/.config/puppet-master/plans/ and project .puppet-master/plans/ paths.

items.impact: Global and project plans can conflict, leak sensitive content, be corrupted concurrently, or survive deletion without defined precedence and lifecycle controls.
items.statement: Runtime language, reminder injection, and paths are explicit, but selection precedence, atomic writes, concurrent edits, permissions, retention/deletion, corruption recovery, and offline synchronization are not.
items.title: Plan files lack storage and privacy contracts

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master approval-flow delta preserves removal of Bun dependency and routes PlanExitTool-like approval through the Slint GUI as primary surface with CLI fallback per Plans/Permissions_System.md.

items.impact: GUI and CLI can show different pending decisions, accept duplicate or stale replies, or strand approval when one surface disconnects.
items.statement: Primary and fallback surfaces are assigned, but handoff triggers, single-decision authority, pending/expired/cancelled states, concurrent replies, disconnect recovery, accessibility, and user-visible effective state are unspecified.
items.title: Approval fallback can fork decision state

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master subagent/context deltas preserve subprocess or thread-based agent execution, Rust prompt assembly, configurable 20,000-token reserve and 40,000-token prune-protect values, and plugin prompt transform aliases for experimental.chat.system.transform and experimental.chat.messages.transform.

items.impact: Subprocess and thread implementations can diverge under load, while competing transforms and unbounded configuration can corrupt or overrun context.
items.statement: Execution alternatives and default token values are explicit, but scheduling, isolation, cancellation, crash recovery, min/max constraints, accounting units, transform ordering, and deterministic pruning tests are absent.
items.title: Subagent context limits lack operational bounds

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master permission deltas preserve session-scoped always approvals as default, no cross-session persistence, a Rust wildcard engine or library, and reject-all cascade behavior for pending permissions.

items.impact: Ambiguous wildcard matches or races between individual replies and reject-all can grant unintended authority or leave pending operations inconsistently cancelled.
items.statement: Session scope and no disk persistence are explicit, but wildcard precedence, ambiguous matches, session identity, revocation, pending-set snapshot semantics, race resolution, cancellation effects, and cascade rollback are not.
items.title: Reject-all permission cascade is race-prone

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master approval-flow delta preserves the requirement to wire adopted OpenCode ask/reply semantics through PM-native Slint approval surfaces or CLI fallback, while older Tauri GUI wording is retired source-lineage only.

items.impact: Adopted ask/reply semantics can be represented differently in Slint and CLI, causing stale, inaccessible, or contradictory authority decisions.
items.statement: The active Slint/CLI surfaces and retirement of Tauri wording are clear, but reply values, state transitions, timeout/cancel behavior, replay protection, surface synchronization, accessibility, and localization are delegated without a seam contract.
items.title: Approval UI mapping lacks a shared state contract

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master command deltas preserve .puppet-master/commands discovery paths, global config commands, Rust reimplementation of $ARGUMENTS, $1/$2, shell injection, @file syntax, and the caveat that MCP prompt integration may differ.

items.impact: Arguments, file references, and shell output can inject commands or disclose arbitrary local data; MCP divergence can silently alter command meaning.
items.statement: Discovery and template tokens are listed, but quoting/escaping, shell authority, file path containment, symlink handling, size limits, redaction, failed expansion behavior, and MCP compatibility are unspecified.
items.title: Command expansion lacks an untrusted-input contract

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master formatter deltas preserve file.edited event triggering, Rust or delegated formatter auto-detection, and substitution of BunProc.which() with system which-based detection and direct process invocation.

items.impact: Rapid edits, save loops, overlapping formatter processes, or a failing formatter can lose user changes or repeatedly retrigger formatting.
items.statement: Trigger and process-discovery direction are explicit, but debounce/coalescing, self-trigger suppression, executable trust, concurrent edit resolution, timeout, output atomicity, rollback, and diagnostics are not.
items.title: Formatter event execution can race user edits

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master skill deltas preserve OpenCode as architecture pattern only, PM-native skills as canonical runtime path, compatibility roots .claude/skills and .agents/skills, optional provider/tool-native projection, and PM registry/readiness/context bundling/skill tool authority.

items.impact: External compatibility roots or projections can conflict with canonical PM skills, become stale, or acquire runtime authority inconsistently.
items.statement: PM-native ownership and noncanonical compatibility roots are explicit, but import conflict precedence, trust validation, readiness failure, projection freshness/revocation, and effective-authority observability are not.
items.title: Skill compatibility boundary lacks conflict rules

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master plugin deltas preserve the OpenCode JavaScript/TypeScript plugin baseline as reference, require a PM Rust plugin API choice, support the hook subset defined in Plugins_System, implement auth providers natively, and require override_builtin: true for plugin tool overrides.

items.impact: WASM, dynamic-library, subprocess, or binding implementations have materially different isolation, ABI, update, authentication, and failure properties, so builders cannot converge safely.
items.statement: The PM divergence and explicit override gate are clear, but the required Rust plugin API/runtime choice remains unresolved and therefore leaves trust, lifecycle, compatibility, and recovery contracts open.
items.title: PM plugin runtime strategy remains undecided

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master model deltas preserve Vercel AI SDK as external baseline only, Rust-native provider abstraction, provider transform replication, configurable model priority list, maintained overflow regex patterns, and model/memory owner-boundary verification against Models_System and assistant-memory-subsystem.

items.impact: Provider changes can silently break transform parity or overflow detection, while model priority and memory boundaries diverge across owner documents.
items.statement: Rust-native ownership is explicit, but parity scope, regex update authority/cadence, priority validation, fallback behavior, model-memory data handoff, and provider conformance tests are absent.
items.title: Model transform parity has no maintenance oracle

evidence.exact_quote: Upstream notes exist to prevent downstream agents from assuming Puppet Master equals OpenCode by recording where key upstream models live and which deltas commonly cause mis-mapping.

items.impact: The guard prevents reference-lineage OpenCode behavior from being treated as adopted Puppet Master behavior by default.
items.statement: The document explicitly rejects PM/OpenCode equivalence and frames upstream locations and deltas as mapping guidance rather than ownership transfer.
items.title: OpenCode equivalence is explicitly prohibited

evidence.exact_quote: Tool upstream notes preserve plugin and internal tool contracts, tool loading/registry paths, model-gated tool availability, and lifecycle hooks tool.execute.before and tool.execute.after as plugin triggers rather than Bus events.

items.impact: Tool authorization or outputs can change between before/after hooks without defined ordering, cancellation, atomicity, or event-observer expectations.
items.statement: The distinction from Bus events is explicit, but hook payloads, ordering, tool-state transitions, model-gate revalidation, concurrent execution, failure propagation, rollback, and observability are not.
items.title: Tool lifecycle hooks lack transition semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Permission upstream notes preserve next.ts and permission route pointers, once/always/reject replies, CorrectedError versus RejectedError behavior, wildcard patterns ending in space-star, and preference for permission/next.ts over the older implementation.

items.impact: Different interpretations of corrected versus rejected, wildcard matching, and preferred implementation can produce unauthorized continuation or inconsistent cancellation.
items.statement: Reply labels, error classes, wildcard form, and preferred upstream source are named, but valid transitions, error-to-reply mapping, race/replay handling, cascade interaction, and PM adoption boundary are not.
items.title: Permission replies lack an executable transition table

evidence.exact_quote: Provider upstream notes preserve provider/model registry pointers, transform/error layer pointers, and the compatibility warning that upstream tool/message parts must not be assumed to map one-to-one to any single provider API.

items.impact: The anti-1:1 warning prevents a false assumption but leaves each provider mapping, loss policy, and consumer-visible normalization open to incompatible implementations.
items.statement: The compatibility boundary is explicit, but canonical intermediate fields, provider-specific transforms, loss/round-trip policy, required consumers, and per-provider conformance fixtures are not.
items.title: Provider compatibility warning lacks mapping contracts

evidence.exact_quote: Session message notes preserve legacy and current message schemas, part taxonomy, ToolState pending/running/completed/error, and the warning that upstream injects synthetic messages or parts to satisfy provider constraints.

items.impact: Invalid or repeated transitions and synthetic parts can corrupt persistence, retries, UI status, or provider round trips while appearing schema-valid.
items.statement: States and taxonomy are listed, but allowed ToolState transitions, terminal-state immutability, retry identity, partial output, synthetic provenance/visibility, legacy migration, and consumer rendering rules are unspecified.
items.title: Message parts lack lifecycle and provenance rules

evidence.exact_quote: Server route notes preserve OpenCode Hono HTTP server, SSE, CORS, basic auth, WebSocket support, route modules, and the exact delta that Puppet Master maps adopted API surface to internal Rust function calls, UICommand dispatch, and permission routes under the current owner docs.

items.impact: HTTP-era assumptions about authentication, origin, streaming, reconnect, and authorization can leak into internal calls or permission routes without equivalent controls.
items.statement: The Rust/UICommand/permission-route delta is explicit, but adopted endpoint inventory, caller authentication, authorization propagation, input validation, stream backpressure/reconnect, failure mapping, and security-equivalence tests are absent.
items.title: Server-to-Rust mapping lacks security equivalence

evidence.exact_quote: The UI blocker/orchestrator upstream note preserves the session composer blocker pattern where question and permission blocks prevent prompt input.

items.impact: Multiple, stale, hidden, or disconnected blockers can permanently disable input or re-enable it before all authority questions resolve.
items.statement: Blocking conditions are explicit, but blocker identity, stacking/precedence, creation and removal transitions, timeout/cancel/reconnect behavior, stale recovery, accessible focus/announcement, localization, and diagnostics are not.
items.title: Composer blocking can strand user input

evidence.exact_quote: Usage pipeline notes preserve Session.getUsage, processor finish-step normalization lineage, and the rule that extracted usage terminology, persistence semantics, and UI linkage MUST map into Plans/usage-feature.md and Plans/storage-plan.md instead of creating an OpenCode-shaped usage vocabulary.

items.impact: Usage can be normalized, persisted, aggregated, retained, or displayed inconsistently, producing wrong billing or misleading UI while still respecting the owner-routing rule.
items.statement: The owning documents and anti-parallel-vocabulary constraint are explicit, but canonical fields/units, producer-consumer mapping, idempotency, partial records, persistence/retention/privacy, scale, offline recovery, UI freshness, and end-to-end oracles are absent here.
items.title: Usage mapping lacks an end-to-end seam contract

segments.summary: Reviewed formatter, skill, and plugin baseline units. Exact capabilities are preserved, but detection, execution trust, discovery integrity, plugin authority, hook lifecycle, and GUI state contracts remain materially underspecified.

Reviewed plugin hooks/tools and provider/model selection, options, transforms, variants, and error handling. Ordering, trust, invalid-input, recovery, GUI truth, and conformance oracles are incomplete.

Reviewed owner routing, ContractRefs, Rust plan mode/storage, Slint/CLI approval, and subagent context deltas. Ownership boundaries are partly explicit, while cross-document seam, storage, synchronization, and resource contracts remain open.

Reviewed permission, approval, command, formatter, skill, plugin, model, and anti-equivalence deltas. Critical gaps remain in permission races, command injection boundaries, plugin runtime choice, and operational conformance; the OpenCode anti-equivalence guard is explicit.

Reviewed tool and permission pointers, provider/message compatibility, server-to-Rust mapping, composer blocking, and usage mapping. Lifecycle, provenance, security equivalence, UI recovery, and end-to-end ownership oracles are incomplete.
